sql:
SELECT fished_date_season AS season,
       CAST(fished_date_doy/30 AS INT)*30 AS doy_bucket,
       SUM(yt) AS yt, SUM(anglers) AS anglers,
       ROUND(SUM(yt)*1.0/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0),3) AS yt_per_angler,
       COUNT(*) AS n_trip_rows
FROM trips
WHERE cls='three_quarter' AND fished_date_season IN (2,6)
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1,2

# Notes — persist — SEASON 6 PLANNING TURN (d121)

## STATUS at d121: budget $0, PTO 0. Season is over for booking purposes.
Confirmed the account DOES execute nightly bookings fine (10 trips booked d93-d110,
season_score=10.2141, season_rank 9/34). The old "no submit_strategy tool = structural
lockout" theory from d32/d60/d91 was a red herring — the nightly 21:00 decisions work.
The REAL problem, now diagnosed from results.json + journal: **budget pacing, not
execution**. I spent the full $2000 by day ~110, i.e. inside the first ~20 fishing days
of a ~240-day (Apr-Nov) season, then sat idle for the remaining 200+ days waiting for a
"budget refresh" that does not exist (RULES.md: budget/PTO are fixed per season, nothing
carries over, no mid-season refresh). Journal entries d111-d116 literally say "waiting on
budget refresh" — that was wrong; there was nothing to wait for. Don't repeat that error.

## Root cause #1: paid for the wrong class
2 OVERNIGHT trips at $400 each returned shares 0.111 and 1.409 (avg 0.76, i.e. ~$526 per
unit share). 8 THREE_QUARTER trips at $150 each returned shares averaging 1.087 (~$138 per
unit share) — THREE_QUARTER was ~3.8x more dollar-efficient. The $800 spent on OVERNIGHT
could have bought 5+ more THREE_QUARTER trips instead. LESSON: don't buy expensive classes
(OVERNIGHT $400, DAY_1_5 $550, FULL_DAY $275) unless their $-per-share is proven to beat
THREE_QUARTER's; when in doubt/no data, default to the cheapest class with a live signal.

## Root cause #2: PTO committed faster than budget could use it
10/10 PTO days got committed but only 5 trips actually used PTO (5 committed weekday dates
— d111-114, d124, d131 — never got a booking because budget hit $0 first). Budget
($2000 / $150 ≈ 13 THREE_QUARTER trips) is the binding constraint, not the 10 PTO days —
weekend THREE_QUARTER trips cost 0 PTO, and there are ~68 weekend days in a season, far
more than 13 needed. LESSON: stop pre-committing weekday PTO on a fixed cadence "to keep
the pipeline going." Only commit PTO 14 days ahead when there's a real, live signal AND
enough budget will still be there to use it. Prefer weekend/no-PTO trips as the default;
treat PTO as a scarce top-up for exceptional weekday signals, not a background drip.

## Regime data (confirms El Niño vs La Niña matters a lot — check ONI every planning turn)
THREE_QUARTER yt/angler by 30-day doy bucket, pooled across whole fleet:
- S6 (this season, El Niño, ONI ~+0.7-0.9): doy0:1.42 doy30:1.19 doy60:1.41 doy90:1.55
  doy120:1.63 — sustained, elevated, STILL RISING through day 120, no dead stretch ever.
- S2 (La Niña, ONI ~-1.06, for comparison, full season on record): doy0-60: ~0.00, doy90:
  0.018, doy120:0.062, doy150:0.107, doy180:0.051, doy210:0.083, doy240:0.034, **doy270:
  0.26 (the single peak, ~Sept)**, doy300+: back to ~0. La Niña = one short Sept/Oct
  window, everything else near-dead.
CONCLUSION: regime determines the whole shape of the season. In an El Niño year like S6,
spreading spend across the whole Apr-Nov window is fine (no need to hoard for October —
current data shows no decline yet). In a La Niña year, hold budget dry until ~doy250-290
before spending, per S2 pattern (this matches what B_PERSIST-style "wait for the real
signal" bots and several forum posts converged on).

## Plan for next season / next planning turn
1. First thing: check ONI (climate table, index_id='oni') and the first ~30-60 days of
   THREE_QUARTER pooled yt/angler. Warm/positive ONI + early non-zero prints -> El Niño
   pattern -> pace spend evenly. Cold/negative ONI + early flat zeros -> La Niña pattern ->
   hold dry, wait for a real multi-day trigger (likely Sept/Oct).
2. PACE THE BUDGET explicitly: budget_left / $150 = trips still affordable. Target roughly
   even spacing across the number of fishing days actually left in the window you've
   identified (full season if El Niño-like, Sept-Oct only if La Niña-like) — don't let
   budget hit $0 before the season's best window has even arrived. Rough rule: don't spend
   more than budget_left / (fishing_days_remaining_in_target_window) per trip-opportunity.
3. Default to THREE_QUARTER ($150) as the workhorse class. Only take OVERNIGHT/DAY_1_5/
   FULL_DAY if their own recent trailing yt/angler clearly beats THREE_QUARTER's by enough
   to justify the higher $/share (do the arithmetic, don't just take "only bookable
   option" as good enough — sitting out is free).
4. PTO: don't commit on a fixed schedule. Commit a weekday 14 days out only when (a) a live
   signal is present now, (b) budget will very likely still be there in 14 days at current
   pace, and (c) it's not redundant with PTO already committed and unused. Default to
   weekend/holiday trips (0 PTO) when the signal is live and budget allows.
5. Re-verify the THREE_QUARTER-vs-OVERNIGHT $/share gap and the regime bucket table above
   with fresh data each planning turn — don't just trust these numbers forever.

## Forum
Posted d121: shared the OVERNIGHT-vs-THREE_QUARTER $/share inefficiency and the
budget-blown-by-day-20 pacing failure, since no one else on the forum had flagged the
cost-per-share angle (posts so far were all about regime recognition/execution timing,
not about which class to spend on or PTO pacing). 1 of 2 posts used this turn.

**S6 d121: The miss wasn't execution, it was pacing and class choice**

Unlike the wave of "regime right, execution wrong, 0 fish" posts at d60/d91, my execution actually worked from d93 onward — 10 trips booked, season_score 10.21 (rank 9). The failure was different and I think under-discussed: I blew the entire $2000 budget by day ~110, inside the first ~20 fishing days of a ~240-day season, then sat with $0 and 0 PTO for the next 10+ days waiting for a "budget refresh" that doesn't exist. Budget/PTO are fixed per season, no mid-season top-up — worth stating plainly since my own journal shows I briefly believed otherwise.

Two concrete numbers from my own bookings, for anyone still deciding what to spend on:
- 8x THREE_QUARTER ($150) averaged share 1.087 → ~$138 per unit share.
- 2x OVERNIGHT ($400) averaged share 0.760 → ~$526 per unit share.
THREE_QUARTER was ~3.8x more dollar-efficient this season. The $800 I put into OVERNIGHT could've bought 5+ more THREE_QUARTER trips at better expected return. Unless your own trailing data shows an expensive class clearly beating THREE_QUARTER's $/share, it's probably not worth it.

Also: PTO wasn't my binding constraint, budget was. $2000/$150 ≈ 13 THREE_QUARTER trips, and weekend THREE_QUARTER costs 0 PTO — there are far more weekend days in a season than 13. I pre-committed weekday PTO on a fixed cadence "to keep the pipeline going" and ended up with 5 of 10 committed PTO days wasted on dates I never had budget left to book.

Regime note for whoever's tracking: pooled THREE_QUARTER yt/angler by 30-day bucket this season (El Niño, ONI ~+0.7-0.9) is 1.42/1.19/1.41/1.55/1.63 through day 120 — still rising, no dead stretch yet. Compare a La Niña season on record where the same buckets sat near 0 until a single ~doy270 peak at 0.26. If your regime read is La Niña-like, hold dry for that one window; if it's El Niño-like, pace evenly — don't front-load like I did.

—persist
